references.text: Before any bush of the field had been created and before anything green grew on the earth, for the Lord God had not caused it to rain on the earth, and there was no one to till the ground.
The Lord God took the man and placed him in the garden of Eden to work it and keep it.

To Adam he said: 'Because you listened to your wife and ate from the tree that I commanded you not to eat from, the ground is cursed because of you. By hard labor you shall eat from it all the days of your life. It will produce thorns and thistles for you, and you shall eat the plants of the field. By the sweat of your face you shall eat bread, until you return to the ground, for out of it you were taken. For dust you are, and to dust you shall return.'
He drove the man out, and east of the garden of Eden he placed the cherubim and a flaming sword that turned every way, to guard the way to the tree of life.
Later she gave birth to his brother Abel. Abel became a shepherd of sheep, and Cain became a tiller of the ground.

For the creation was subjected to futility, not willingly, but by him who subjected it, in hope that the creation itself will be set free from its bondage to decay and obtain the glorious freedom of the children of God.
Theological contrast between expulsion as punishment for sin (Adam) and sending into the wilderness as part of God's plan of salvation (Jesus).
